current_example.problem: If $x + 8 \equiv 11\: (\textrm{mod}\,15),$ find an equivalent statement where $x$ is isolated.
current_example.worked_solution:
The addition property of congruences states that 

$$
a\equiv b  \quad \Longleftrightarrow\quad a+c\equiv b+c \qquad (\textrm{mod}\,n).
$$

Similarly, the subtraction property states that

$$
a\equiv b \quad \Longleftrightarrow\quad a-c\equiv b-c \qquad (\textrm{mod}\,n).
$$

We use the subtraction property to subtract $8$ from both sides of the given congruence, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+8 & ≡11\, & (\text{mod}\,15) \\ x+8-8 & ≡11-8\, & (\text{mod}\,15) \\ x & ≡3\, & (\text{mod}\,15)\end{aligned}
$$
